# Housekeeping: builtins-compiler

## Authorized scope and smallest closable slice

Review the complete `crates/builtins-compiler` Cargo package and its tests. Deliver practical, behavior-preserving cleanup in this package, or an evidenced no-change verdict when existing choices earn their cost. Cover all five user requests: repeated code/LoC; load-bearing test purposes; avoidable copies; applicable micro SIMD; and data structures that cap efficiency. The user requests two GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh agents concurrently; this overrides the default Terra implementation model for this workflow. Root Sol owns briefing, adversarial review, exact-path checkpoints, integration and remote synchronization.

## Frozen boundaries

Existing public APIs, feature behavior, canonical/wire identities, arithmetic order and per-lane rendered bits, latency/tail, link modes, smoothing and NaN/denormal rules remain contractual. Zero render allocations/frees, locks, I/O or syscalls; no runtime native ISA dispatch. Retain scalar tails, 4-lane Wasm/NEON and x86 AVX2/FMA. Preserve all feature and target configurations. Do not expand another open issue or change DSP algorithms. Read current related issue bodies before touching their subject; discoveries that require architecture or product decisions become bounded follow-ups and final owner questions.

## Implementation and test-value decisions

Prefer deleting or consolidating repetition to adding abstractions that increase total complexity. Assess every existing test or a clearly named homogeneous family by its plausible unique defect; remove trivial, redundant or obsolete cases only after identifying the surviving behavioral gate. Keep independent numeric/oracle, fault, allocation, queue, boundary and target tests. Add/rewrite tests only for a concrete uncovered defect, and state which plausible defect no existing test catches. No prose/source-grep tests, new bit-digest pins or exact resource-byte pins. Copies needed for ownership, snapshots or atomic admission stay unless the same semantics are proved with less work. Data structure changes must preserve deterministic order and bounded realtime work. Inspect applicable hot loops and generated code before claiming additional SIMD; recursive/stateful dependencies alone do not justify changing arithmetic.

## Objective gates and evidence

- Read all production and test files in this package; record concise findings for each of the five requests, concrete changed/deferred locations, and load-bearing test families with retained coverage for deletions.
- Run focused locked package tests and affected feature configurations; use existing downstream/RT/differential gates proportional to the changed contract. Check formatting and package clippy with warnings denied. Relevant Wasm and AArch64 compile checks are required for changed product code; record limitations candidly.
- Changes to DSP arithmetic or hot state need existing independent numeric and scalar/SIMD gates plus one-time base/head evidence when needed; no permanent comparison against the old implementation. Existing research remains the algorithm authority; no new algorithm or listening claim is authorized.
- Benchmarks are optional and descriptive. Any timed measurement freezes its workload/validator, passes zero-workload preflight, and runs exactly one invocation with one warmup/two measured rounds. No timing optimization loop, performance percentage or unsupported sound-quality claim.
- Root conducts one adversarial verdict per coherent attempt, at most five total attempts. Every new/rewritten test gets its unique-defect sentence in that verdict. No-change audits require the same five-axis review, not manufactured edits.
- Stop after a coherent compiling, focused-green tranche; root commits exact owned paths before further edits. Keep edits within `crates/builtins-compiler` and this numbered spec. Independent crates use separate worktrees. Root pushes promptly and updates this GitHub issue with evidence; close only after PASS and evidence upstream, verifying remote state. Merge through the required qualification check and remove clean completed worktrees.

## Sol brief approval and decision record

Approved 2026-10-01 by root Sol within the user's crate-by-crate housekeeping request. Attempt 1 is authorized with the frozen scope/gates above. Owner questions are collected for the final report; routine reversible cleanup proceeds autonomously. Scope is this package's housekeeping, not completion of pre-existing feature/bug issues.

## Attempt evidence

### Attempt 1 — implementation checkpoint `9a969b36`

Worker B (GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh) read the complete package production source, inline tests, six integration files and mutation history. Related scopes reviewed: #953 (default test helper gating), #1053 (bounded concurrent fader/matrix drains), #931 (graph arena colouring), #891/#890 (input symmetry/fader-matrix kernels), #899 (PDC copies), #882/#951 (meter delivery/held-peak banking), and the existing live-control/symmetry rulings. Those product outcomes remain separate.

Five-axis findings:

- **Repetition/LoC:** remove the mutation matrix's transcript formatting/hash, self completion counter and historical layout repin commentary; retain the generator, seed, 10,000 inputs in the same order, all 49 classes and behavioral/diversity assertions. Reuse `processor_seal` for borrowed validation and owned preparation identities. Net package Rust change: **−147 lines** (51 added, 198 removed).
- **Test value:** two strict subset/constant tests removed; one duplicated ABI membership traversal removed. Concrete survivor mapping and all retained families are below. No new tests or historical reference implementation/output pins.
- **Copies:** dependency-level map keys, bank-member lookups, meter duplicate keys and temporary expected/actual track, processor and control identities now borrow their existing owners. Owned session seals, graph IDs, diagnostics, queue endpoints and independent transactional snapshots remain owned; no retained resource layout or public API changes. Iterator equality checks lengths as well as values, so missing/extra/duplicate tuples are still refused.
- **Micro SIMD:** changed helpers do ordered string comparisons and control-plane indexing; no DSP arithmetic/helper is factored. Fresh native production release assembly (`cargo rustc --locked -p builtins-compiler --lib --release -- --emit=asm`) shows input/fader/matrix/composite processors calling `BuiltinInputBank::process`, `BuiltinFaderBank::process`, `BuiltinMatrixBank::process` and the settled fusion bridge. The compiler adapters contain no packed sample arithmetic to vectorize; W4/W8 arithmetic belongs to `builtins`, and scalar/reference paths remain under test support. No additional SIMD, assembly-copy improvement or timing claim is made.
- **Data structures:** retain deterministic BTreeMap/BTreeSet ordering and the single cohort planner, while borrowing temporary map keys. Review also found `expected_tails` checking every control for every track, leaving O(tracks × controls) membership work; this is the bounded attempt-2 correction below.

**Root adversarial verdict: REQUEST CHANGES.** Other changes were accepted as coherent; correct the tail membership scan by reusing the already-required sorted borrowed control vector, without a second set or public API/DSP change.

- **Source-set binding (3):** successful single ownership, every prevalidation error, and delegated failure restoration detect dropped/doubled owners or private/external mispartitioning; report, source telemetry and eventual drops are checked.
- **Bank layout/resources (2):** dependency waves, sorted members, scalar refusal, full/partial W4/W8 groups and independently derived two-plane/actual-member charges detect regrouping, padding and admission misaccounting.
- **Actual scalar adjacent/split graph families:** selection and overlap precedence, output-track eligibility, intervening observer failures, pending-fader materialization, ramp/retarget/retry at F_A/F_B/M_A/M_B and queued-prefix/tail handling defend distinct schedule/ownership/error boundaries. Extra readers, aliases, nonunity sends, actual effect sidechains and staggered observed peers retain separate owners and exact current-reference PCM/state/meter results.
- **Direct scalar owner families:** exact concrete types and both delivery policies, deferred settled fader, invalid begin/pair envelopes, untouched later matrix queue and reset equivalence defend factory refusal and direct-call states unavailable through valid render envelopes.
- **Actual banked pair families:** serialized selection versus concurrent separate owners, post-fader observer/cohort refusal, send and alias-observer barriers assert the real selected mechanism as well as current PCM/meter equivalence; PCM equality alone cannot catch lost fusion admission.
- **Direct composite/factory families:** full/partial widths, FIFO/immediate commands, short/long ramps, retarget/mute/reset, false-bridge nonmutation and malformed raw records preserve arithmetic order. Wrong concrete types/order, concurrent policy, width/population mismatch and returned queued owner/state gates protect independent refusal paths. The three-sample/two-call gate retains the exact ramp crossing boundary.
- **Delivery metadata (2) and scalar resource formula (1):** default/concurrent/serialized and selected-meter wrappers cannot accidentally share policy; real owner sizes and the larger split outer/table reservation independently constrain charged storage.
- **Resident metering (2):** accepted versus forced-planar paths compare every snapshot word, aliases/mixed custom observers/delayed nonunity sends, nonfinite input, queue overflow and failure ordering; the focused acceptance gate additionally rejects unnecessary planar acquisition during collapse/fallback transitions.
- **Scalar/bank/track-count identity (2):** distinct nonsilent per-track signals detect wrong lane coefficients, gather/scatter/padding and cross-track coupling; session-count comparison also catches changes shared by each session's scalar and vector preparation.
- **Preparation/validation:** every named meter tap, three section ownership, controlled infinite versus disabled plain zero tail, duplicate/unknown meter/control errors, missing strip and attached producer sealing retain contract-specific gates. Largest/state/meter one-below caps and independent hard-bit cutoff/successor limits at all four launch rates protect admission and exact numeric diagnostics; the 49-class mutation family remains as described above.
- **Automation ABI (3):** independent full session/descriptor table equality, fixed launch live/prepared IDs, and the wire vocabulary `strip` detect metadata drift, simultaneous liveness drift or renamed contract identity.
- **Input records (5):** 64-byte slot ceiling, every selector/variant event, composed LIVE/agreement clearing, latch after re-equalization and capacity-filled/wrapped scalar/banked drains protect storage, symmetry and complete next-block application.
- **Allocator integration (10 active):** direct W4 composite, native banked/queued scalar/split/input-trim and actual runtime-bank paths independently measure zero render allocations/frees. Retained owner/table/conversion allowances, failure completion, off-render release, measured layout/report equality, first-touch ceiling and repeated observations protect accounting and instrumentation validity.
- **Large metered preparation (1), delay contract (2), nightly scale (2 ignored):** 256 tracks/56 meters test cross-track address-free preparation order/repeatability; schema/descriptor delay equality and absence of duplicate builtin delay charging remain independent. ### Attempt 2 — bounded tail lookup correction, checkpoint `db90ad42`

Move collection/sort of the existing borrowed `(track_id, capacity)` control vector before tail derivation; use binary search by ID in the private tail helper. IDs are primary tuple sort keys, so duplicates (even different capacities) and unknown IDs retain the old membership result. Control mismatch diagnostics still occur in their original position; chain preparation and tail sorting/ownership are unchanged. This removes O(tracks × controls) searches in favour of O(tracks × log controls), sharing the pre-existing O(controls × log controls) sort and vector. No second index allocation; empty controls stay an empty vector. Net Rust LoC remains **−147** relative to the issue base.

Focused revision checks: all **51** all-feature package unit tests and the downstream forged-seal gate pass again; `cargo clippy --locked -p builtins-compiler --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, workspace formatting and diff validation pass (the same configuration warnings above). Production target, package release, integration/policy and unchanged-hot-path evidence above remain applicable; no matrix replay or additional product edits. Ready for root's evidence checkpoint and single attempt-2 verdict.

### Root adversarial review — attempt 2

Root adversarial verdict: PASS for the frozen housekeeping scope. Root reviewed every production/test diff and the narrow lookup revision. Referent string/GraphNodeId ordering equals the former owned ordering; iterator equality still rejects length mismatches and duplicates. Owned seals and returned owners stay intact. Tuple sorting puts IDs first, so binary-search membership preserves duplicate/different-capacity/unknown-name behavior; the sole private caller supplies the sorted view and emits diagnostics at the original positions. This reuses a required allocation/sort rather than adding a second index, reducing membership searches from quadratic to logarithmic per track. No DSP/helper arithmetic, public feature, resource layout or realtime drain policy changed. Proportional package, target, downstream forged-seal and focused revision gates support this result; no timing percentage is claimed.

Test value: the rewritten 49-class mutation family rejects combinations of launch rate, quantum, tap, smoothing, resource/domain/error and block shape that directed cutoff/allocation cases do not reach; generator/order and every behavioral/diversity assertion remain, while description/debug-layout hash and self count defend no product behavior. The fixed launch-target gate catches simultaneous schema/descriptor drift that their full table equality cannot catch, retaining live trim/polarity and preparation-only delay. Deleted event-equivalence and SEAM-constant checks have stronger selector/composition/live-graph consequences. No new test was added; all allocation/fault/reference and meaningful scale families remain. Existing default test failure #953 and replenishable drains #1053 are explicit separate scopes, so this PASS does not claim they are fixed.
